narrative.intro: Bath Iron Works has $2.1B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Bath Iron Works received 19 awards so far, with an average award size of $112M, and obligations are down 10.3% year over year. Ship Building and Repairing is the dominant market for Bath Iron Works, totaling $2.1B in FY2026 to date. Smaller NAICS entries include Measuring, Dispensing, and Other Pumping Equipment Manufacturing at $37.6K, Convention and Trade Show Organizers at $27K, Commercial, Industrial, and Institutional Electric Lighting Fixture Manufacturing at $25.5K, Hardware Manufacturing at $19K, and Other Metal Valve and Pipe Fitting Manufacturing at $4.2K. Obligations by fiscal year show a climb from $1B in FY21 to $1.3B in FY22, then to $2.1B in FY23 and FY24, a peak of $2.4B in FY25, and $2.1B in FY26. The current-year totals are partial, covering the fiscal year to date. The figures reported are contract obligations except where table notes specify award-value totals for largest awards and expiring contracts.

sections.heading: Who are Bath Iron Works' biggest markets?
sections.body: Ship Building and Repairing is the biggest market for Bath Iron Works, accounting for $2.1B in FY2026 to date. Other identified markets are much smaller, including Measuring, Dispensing, and Other Pumping Equipment Manufacturing at $37.6K and Convention and Trade Show Organizers at $27K. Bath Iron Works also shows Commercial, Industrial, and Institutional Electric Lighting Fixture Manufacturing at $25.5K, Hardware Manufacturing at $19K, and Other Metal Valve and Pipe Fitting Manufacturing at $4.2K.

sections.heading: How have Bath Iron Works' obligations changed over recent fiscal years?
sections.body: Bath Iron Works' obligations rose from $1B in FY21 to $1.3B in FY22, then to $2.1B in FY23 and FY24 and $2.4B in FY25, before registering $2.1B in FY26. Bath Iron Works' obligations are down 10.3% year over year in the current fiscal-year-to-date reporting. The current-year totals are partial and cover the fiscal year to date.
